sources: IDF announcement + Defence Minister Israel Katz (KAN interview, via AFP); Hebron Deputy Mayor Khaled Fahd al-Qawasmi via Haaretz; Association for Civil Rights in Israel
fault_line: Targeted security operation after two soldiers were killed vs collective punishment timed to sway the Oct 27 election.

sections.what_happened: Hebron Deputy Mayor Khaled Fahd al-Qawasmi told Haaretz on Sunday morning that the IDF has forcibly displaced 2,231 Palestinians (373 families) from their homes in Hebron since the weekend, with ~30 more families threatened. Defence Minister Israel Katz told KAN the displaced "will not be allowed to return... until we've finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron". The IDF announced a general closure: Palestinian workers barred from Israeli communities in the West Bank and Jordan Valley from Sunday and Monday (industrial zones excepted in part), and a ban on entry/exit of Palestinian workers plus closure of all land crossings on election day Tuesday Oct 27. Netanyahu vowed an operation "on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967". The Association for Civil Rights in Israel called the removals, demolitions and closure collective punishment and demanded a halt. Hebron schools are suspended Sunday-Monday; Hebron University and Al-Quds Open University moved Sunday classes online.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct declared-tier families: IDF/Israeli government (T1, STATE IL) for the closure order; AFP (T1) for Katz quote and closure; Haaretz (T3) for the 2,231/373 municipal count. CNBC TV18 adds IDF operated in 400+ locations and detained ~40 people over the weekend (undeclared tier, not counted).
sections.what_disputed: IDF frames the operation as precise, targeted searches for militants/weapons and demolitions in the attackers' area, with ~40 suspects detained; Haaretz notes a general election-day closure is a recurring procedure, so the Oct 27 closure is not solely Hebron-driven. The Palestinian Authority calls the operation collective punishment; Hebron municipality calls it politically motivated. The two attackers were killed Friday; Hamas hailed the attack without claiming it.
sections.why_matters: Election-eve Hebron: 2,231 people out, gates shut until Tuesday. Security crackdown — or a show of force two days before the vote?
